# Apify API

The Apify API (version 2) provides programmatic access to the Apify platform. The API is organized around RESTful HTTP endpoints.

You can download the complete OpenAPI schema of Apify API in the YAML or JSON formats. The source code is also available on GitHub.

All requests and responses (including errors) are encoded in JSON format with UTF-8 encoding, with a few exceptions that are explicitly described in the reference.

To access the API, we recommend using one of our API clients:

Stable API clients:

- For Node.js, we recommend the apify-client NPM package.
- For Python, we recommend the apify-client PyPI package.

Experimental API clients:

- For Java, we recommend the `apify-client` Maven central component.
- For Rust, we recommend the `apify-client` crate.
- For .NET, we recommend the `apify-client` Nuget package.
- For PHP, we recommend the `apify-client` Packagist package.
- For Go, we recommend the `apify-client` package.

The clients' functions correspond to the API endpoints and have the same parameters. This simplifies development of apps that depend on the Apify platform.

Important Request Details

- `Content-Type` header: For requests with a JSON body, you must include the `Content-Type: application/json` header.
- Method override: You can override the HTTP method using the `method` query parameter. This is useful for clients that can only send `GET` requests. For example, to call a `POST` endpoint, append `?method=POST` to the URL of your `GET` request.

## Authentication

You can create an API token on the Integrations page in the Apify Console. The Console shows the token only once, right after you create or rotate it, so copy it and store it somewhere safe. For details, see API token.

To use your token in a request, either:

- (Recommended) Add the token to your request's `Authorization` header as `Bearer `. E.g., `Authorization: Bearer xxxxxxx`. For details, see the Authorization header on MDN.
- Add it as the `token` parameter to your request URL. (Less secure).

Using your token in the request header is more secure than using it as a URL parameter because URLs are often stored in browser history and server logs. This creates a chance for someone unauthorized to access your API token.

Never share your API token or password with untrusted parties!

For more information, see our integrations documentation.

### Agentic payments

AI agents can authenticate and pay for Actor runs without an Apify account using agentic payments. Instead of an API token, the request carries a payment credential that both authorizes and pays for the call. Apify supports the x402 protocol (`PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` header) and Skyfire (`skyfire-pay-id` header).

Agents can also pay once with x402 or the Machine Payments Protocol (MPP) and receive a temporary API token with a fixed spend cap from the Apify Agent General Interface (AGI) at https://agi.apify.com. Use that token as a regular `Bearer` token.

## Basic usage

To run an Actor, send a POST request to the Run Actor endpoint using either the Actor ID code (e.g. `vKg4IjxZbEYTYeW8T`) or its name (e.g. `janedoe~my-actor`):

`https://api.apify.com/v2/actors/[actor_id]/runs`

If the Actor is not runnable anonymously, you will receive a 401 or 403 response code. This means you need to add your secret API token to the request's `Authorization` header (recommended) or as a URL query parameter `?token=[your_token]` (less secure).

Optionally, you can include the query parameters described in the Run Actor section to customize your run.

If you're using Node.js, the best way to run an Actor is using the `Apify.call()` method from the Apify SDK. It runs the Actor using the account you are currently logged into (determined by the secret API token). The result is an Actor run object and its output (if any).

...

## Referring to resources

There are three main ways to refer to a resource you're accessing via API.

- the resource ID (e.g. `iKkPcIgVvwmztduf8`)
- `username~resourcename` - when using this access method, you will need to use your API token, and access will only work if you have the correct permissions.
- `~resourcename` - for this, you need to use an API token, and the `resourcename` refers to a resource in the API token owner's account.

## Authentication

- HTTP: Bearer Auth
- API Key: apiKey

Bearer token provided in the `Authorization` header (e.g., `Authorization: Bearer your_token`—recommended). For details, see the Authorization header on MDN.

Use your API token to authenticate requests. You can create one on the Integrations page in Apify Console. The Console shows the token only once, right after you create or rotate it, so copy it and store it somewhere safe. This method is more secure than query parameters, as headers are not logged in browser history or server logs.

Security

Do not share your API token (or account password) with untrusted parties.

When is authentication required?

- Required for private Actors, tasks, or resources (e.g., builds of private Actors).
- Required when using named formats for IDs (e.g., `username~store-name` for stores or `username~queue-name` for queues).
- Optional for public Actors or resources (e.g., builds of public Actors can be queried without a token).

For more information, see our integrations documentation.

auth.title: API integration
highlights:
All aspects of the Apify platform can be controlled via a REST API, which is described in detail in the API Reference. If you want to use the Apify API from JavaScript/Node.js or Python, we strongly recommend using one of the API clients:

- apify-client `npm` package for JavaScript, supporting both browser and server
- apify-client PyPI package for Python.

You are not required to those packages - the REST API works with any HTTP client - but the official API clients implement best practices such as exponential backoff and rate limiting.

## API token

To access the Apify API in your integrations, you need to authenticate using your secret API token. You manage your tokens on the API & Integrations page in Apify Console. Give each token a reasonable description, and never use one token for several services, much like you shouldn't use the same password for different accounts.

Apify Console shows the value of an API token only once, right after you create or rotate it. The token list shows each token's description, a masked preview of its value, when it was last used, and when it expires, but you can't view or copy the full value of an existing token.

The Apify CLI doesn't need a copied token. When you sign in with apify login in the browser, it creates a token for your device and stores it for you.

Protect your API token

Do not share the API token with untrusted parties, or use it directly from client-side code, unless you fully understand the consequences! You can also consider limiting the permission scope of the token, so that it can only access what it really needs.

### Create an API token

1. Go to Settings > API & Integrations in Apify Console.
2. In the Personal API tokens section, select Create a new token.
3. Enter a description. Optionally, limit the token's permissions or set an expiration date.
4. Select Create.
5. Copy the token and store it somewhere safe, such as a password manager.
6. Select Done.

If you lose a token, rotate it to get a new value, or create a new token and delete the old one.

## Authentication

You can authenticate the Apify API in two ways. You can either pass the token via the `Authorization` HTTP header or the URL `token` query parameter. We always recommend you use the authentication via the HTTP header as this method is more secure.

Note that some API endpoints, such as Get list of key-value store keys, do not require an authentication token because they contain a hard-to-guess identifier that effectively serves as an authentication key.

## Expiration

API tokens include security features to protect your account and data. You can set an expiration date for your API tokens, ensuring they become invalid after a specified period. This is particularly useful for temporary access or when working with third-party services.

## Rotation

If you suspect that a token has been compromised or accidentally exposed, you can rotate it through Apify Console. When rotating a token, you have the option to keep the old token active for 24 hours, allowing you to update your applications with the new token before the old one becomes invalid. After the rotation period, the token will be regenerated, and any applications connected to the old token will need to be updated with the new token to continue functioning.

After you confirm the rotation, Apify Console shows the new token. This is the only time you can copy it, so store it somewhere safe.

For better security awareness, the UI marks tokens identified as compromised with a Leaked label, making it easy to identify and take action on them.

## Organization accounts

When working under an organization account, you will see two types of API tokens on the API & Integrations page.

The Personal API tokens are different from your own Personal API tokens mentioned above. If you use this token in an integration, it will have the same permissions that you have within the organization, and all the operations you use it for will be ascribed to you.

On the other hand the Organization API tokens (only visible if you are the owner or have Manage access tokens permission) have full permissions and are not tied to a specific member of the organization.

## API tokens with limited permissions

By default, tokens can access all data in your account. If that is not desirable, you can choose to limit the permissions of your token, so that it can only access data needed for the particular use case. We call these tokens scoped.

A scoped token can access only those resources that you'll explicitly allow it to.

Actor modification restrictions

We do not allow scoped tokens to create or modify Actors. If you do need to create or modify Actors through the Apify API, use an unscoped token.

### How to create a scoped token

Scoped tokens behave like standard API tokens and are managed through the API & Integrations page in Apify Console. When creating a token (or updating an existing one), simply toggle "Limit token permissions" to make the token scoped.

Once the token is scoped, you can specify the token's permissions.

### Account-level vs resource-specific permissions

We support two different types of permissions for tokens:

- Account-level permissions: These will apply to all resources in the entire account. For example, you can use these to allow the token to run all your Actors.
- Resource-specific permissions: These will apply only to specific, existing resources. For example, you can use these to allow the token to read from a particular dataset.

auth.title: Apify MCP server
highlights:
## Prerequisites

...

- An Apify account - You need one unless your agent uses only the tools that work without an account or pays through agentic payments. Sign up for an Apify account, if you don't have one.
- ... This could be claude.ai, Claude Desktop, VS Code with MCP support, or any application that implements the MCP specification. The official MCP documentation maintains a list of compatible clients.
- Apify API token (optional) - Only needed for the local stdio server or the Bearer token option. The recommended remote connection signs you in with OAuth instead. Create an API token in Apify Console.

## Connect and authorize

To discover Actors and search the documentation, you can connect without an account. To run Actors, connect in one of two ways: use the hosted Apify service with Streamable HTTP with OAuth, or run the server locally for development and testing with local stdio.

...

### Use without an account

The Apify MCP server accepts requests without an API token when the `tools` query parameter (see Tool selection) contains only tools enabled for unauthenticated use. These tools cover Actor discovery, documentation lookup, and the Apify API reference:

- `search-actors`
- `fetch-actor-details`
- `search-apify-docs`
- `fetch-apify-docs`
- `apify-api-search`
- `apify-api-details`

For example, the following URL connects without authentication:

`https://mcp.apify.com?tools=search-actors,fetch-actor-details,search-apify-docs,fetch-apify-docs`

If the `tools` parameter includes any other tool, or you connect to the default endpoint, the server requires an API token. Running Actors and accessing storage or run data always requires authentication, so use one of the methods below when you're ready to run Actors.

### Streamable HTTP with OAuth (recommended)

Add `https://mcp.apify.com` to your MCP client. On first connection, your browser opens so you can sign in to Apify and approve access. To authorize without signing in, use your Apify API token instead.

OAuth

This flow authorizes the server without putting your API token in the client configuration.

```json
{

  "mcpServers": {

    "apify": {

      "url": "https://mcp.apify.com"

    }

  }

}

```

Bearer token

You can also use your Apify token directly, instead of OAuth, by setting the `Authorization: Bearer ` header in the MCP server configuration.

```json
{

  "mcpServers": {

    "apify": {

      "url": "https://mcp.apify.com",

      "headers": {

        "Authorization": "Bearer <APIFY_TOKEN>"

      }

    }

  }

}

```

Replace `` with your Apify API token.

For a client-specific configuration, use the MCP configurator: pick the Actors and tools you need, then copy the generated configuration into your client. If you use the Apify CLI, `apify mcp install ` writes the configuration for you, for example `apify mcp install cursor`.

n8n is an open source, fair-code licensed tool for workflow automation.

...

This integration uses a third-party service. If you find outdated content, please submit an issue on GitHub.

Once installed, the next step is authentication.

## Authentication

The Apify node offers two authentication methods to securely connect to your Apify account. Choose based on your setup - API key works for both self-hosted and cloud instances, while OAuth2 is cloud-only.

### API Key (cloud & self-hosted instance)

1. In the n8n Editor UI, click on Create Credential.
2. Search for Apify API and click Continue.
3. Enter your Apify API token. (find it in the Apify Console).
4. Click Save.

### OAuth2 (cloud instance only)

1. In n8n Cloud, select Create Credential.
2. Search for Apify OAuth2 API and select Continue.
3. Select Connect my account and authorize with your Apify account.
4. n8n automatically retrieves and stores the OAuth2 tokens.

Credential Control

For simplicity on n8n Cloud, use the API key method if you prefer manual control over credentials.

With authentication set up, you can now create workflows that incorporate the Apify node.

...

## Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues, start by double-checking basics.

- Authentication errors: Verify your API token or OAuth2 settings in Credentials.

highlights:
# Apify Pricing

Flexible plans with pay-as-you-go usage on top of the monthly fee. See apify.com/pricing for the full interactive pricing page.

This page is the pricing reference. How an agent connects to Apify, authenticates, and pays, including with no account and nobody to sign in, is in the agent quickstart at apify.com/agents.md.

## Plans

Save 10% on paid plans when billed annually.

| Plan | Monthly price | Annual price / month | Included usage / month | Apify Store discount | Support |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Free | $0 | $0 | $5 | No Apify Store discount | Community support |
| Starter | $19 | $17 | $19 | Bronze Apify Store discount | Chat support |
| Scale | $199 | $179 | $199 | Silver Apify Store discount | Priority chat support |
| Business | $999 | $899 | $999 | Gold Apify Store discount | Account manager |

Building and publishing your own Actors? The Creator plan costs $1 / month and comes with a one-time $500 of platform usage for the first 6 months, but limits Apify Store to universal Actors. See apify.com/pricing/creator-plan.md.

## Actor runs

Most Actors in Apify Store use pay-per-event pricing, listed on each Actor's page. Pay-per-usage Actors and your own Actors bill platform usage instead, and some pay-per-event Actors charge both. Compute is measured in compute units (CUs). 1 CU = 1 GB of RAM running for 1 hour.

| Plan | CU price | Max RAM | Max concurrent runs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Free | $0.2 / CU | 16 GB | 5 |
| Starter | $0.2 / CU | 64 GB | 32 |
| Scale | $0.16 / CU | 256 GB | 128 |
| Business | $0.13 / CU | 512 GB | 256 |

### How pricing works

Examples on the $19 Starter plan. The plan covers the first $19 of usage each month, and the rest is pay as you go, up to a usage limit you set (at most $100 on Starter).

- Pay per event, for example Instagram Scraper. It charges $2.30 for 1,000 results, so 10,000 results cost $23.
- Pay per usage, for example Website Content Crawler. You pay only for the platform usage of the run: compute units ($0.2 per CU on Starter), proxy, and storage.
- Pay per event + usage, for example Google Trends Scraper. It charges $1 for 1,000 results plus the platform usage of the run, so 20,000 results cost $20 plus usage.

...

### What is the prepaid platform usage, and how much do I need?

The Apify platform has a number of services that are charged based on usages, such as Actors, proxies, data transfer, and storage. See pricing for the full list of platform services.

Each subscription plan comes with a certain amount of prepaid platform usage that is used to pay for services. If your platform usage in a given billing cycle exceeds this prepaid amount, the excess usage will be added to your next invoice, and you'll get a notification. If you're on the free plan, your access to Apify's services will be blocked until the beginning of the next monthly cycle.

Note that unused usage credits are not rolled over to the next billing cycle, and they expire at the end of the billing cycle.

### Can I try Apify for free?

Absolutely! We offer a free plan that lets you use most of the features of the Apify platform, but with certain limits. No credit card is required. The free plan includes Apify Proxy, which is limited to use within the platform and does not extend to external clients.

If you'd like a free demo of Apify's custom solutions, please contact us.

...

### What is the pricing for Actors in Apify Store?

Every Actor in Apify Store uses one of two pricing models, and each Actor's page states which one applies to it.

Pay per event - you pay a fixed price for the events the Actor's developer defines, such as starting the Actor or returning a single result. Most pay-per-event Actors include the Apify platform usage in the event price, but some charge for it separately, so check the pricing section on the Actor's page.

Pay per usage - the developer charges nothing on top, and you only pay for the platform usage consumed by the Actor's runs: compute units, data transfer, storage operations, and residential or SERP proxies.

Both models draw on the platform usage credits included in your plan, and excess usage is charged to your next invoice. Reading from or writing to a run's dataset after the run finishes also counts as platform usage.

gate.title: Apify
highlights:
AI agents reach Apify in three ways. An interactive agent connects the MCP server at https://mcp.apify.com and signs in through the browser. Code that outlives the session — a server, a scheduled job, a product feature — uses the `apify-client` package or the REST API with an API token. An autonomous agent with a wallet and nobody to sign in buys a prepaid, spend-capped token at https://agi.apify.com through x402 or MPP. The quickstart at https://apify.com/agents.md walks through all three.

Important notes:

- No account is needed to explore. Search the Store with `GET https://api.apify.com/v2/store?search={keywords}`, read any Actor by appending `.md` to its page URL, or connect the anonymous MCP tools at https://mcp.apify.com/?tools=search-actors,fetch-actor-details,search-apify-docs,fetch-apify-docs. Running Actors and reading private run or storage data requires authentication.
- Don't guess Actor IDs or API paths: a guess returns a 404. Take the ID from Store search: use the result's `id`, or join `username` and `name` as `username~actor-name` in API URLs. The owner is often not `apify` (Google Maps is `compass/crawler-google-places`). An Actor's input schema is in `data.actorDefinition.input` of `GET https://api.apify.com/v2/actors/{username}~{actor-name}/builds/default`, with no token needed for a public Actor.
- Creating an account is free and requires no credit card: the free plan renews $5 of usage credit every month, and if that credit runs out, access pauses until the next month instead of being billed. There is nothing to cancel.
- If a request fails because nobody is signed in, including a 402 that offers x402 payment, tell the user how to fix it instead of stopping: connect https://mcp.apify.com and sign in through the browser first; otherwise create a token at https://console.apify.com/settings/integrations and set it as an environment variable rather than pasting it into chat.

# Affiliates

The Apify Affiliate Program offers you a way to earn recurring commissions while helping others discover automation and web scraping solutions. Whether you promote Apify Store or refer customers to Apify's professional services, you can monetize your expertise and network.

The program rewards collaboration with up to 30% recurring commission and up to $2,500 per customer for professional services referrals. With no time limits on commissions, transparent tracking, and flexible payout options, it's built for long-term partnerships.

---

## How the program works

The Apify Affiliate Program lets you promote three main offerings:

1. Apify Store: recommend Actors from the marketplace that help businesses automate lead generation, pricing intelligence, content aggregation, and more.
2. The Apify platform: promote the platform's features, including scheduling, monitoring, data export options, proxies, and integrations.
3. Professional services: refer customers who need custom web scraping solutions to Apify's Professional Services team and earn up to $2,500 per closed deal.

### Commission structure

- 20% commission for the first 3 months of each customer's subscription
- 30% commission from month 4 onwards for as long as they remain customers
- Up to $2,500 per customer for professional services referrals
- No time limits on commissions - you earn as long as your referrals stay active

### Free trial advantage

Apify offers a $5 free trial that renews monthly, giving your referrals time to test the tools before subscribing. This increases conversion rates and helps you earn more consistent commissions.

---

## Payment and tracking

### Transparent dashboard

Track referrals in real-time through a dashboard that shows:

- Active referrals
- Commission earnings
- Conversion rates
- Payment history

### Payment options

Receive payouts via:

- Bank transfer
- PayPal

You'll receive your first payment within 30 days of your first successful referral.

...

1. Sign up through the Apify Affiliate program page
2. Access your unique tracking links and promotional materials
3. Start sharing with your network
4. Monitor your referrals and earnings through the dashboard

mcp.title: Apify MCP server
highlights:
# Apify MCP server

The Apify's MCP server (mcp.apify.com) allows AI applications and agents to interact with the Apify platform using Model Context Protocol (MCP). The MCP server enables AI agents to discover and run Actors from Apify Store, access storages and results, and enables AI coding assistants to access Apify documentation and tutorials.

To connect a coding agent such as Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, or Codex, install the Apify plugin instead. It sets up this server together with Agent Skills in one step.

Apify MCP server vs MCP connectors

This page covers the Apify MCP server, which exposes Apify Actors as tools to outside AI clients. If you are building an Actor that needs to call third-party MCP servers (such as Notion or Slack) on a user's behalf, see MCP connectors instead.

## Apify AI vs the MCP server

The Apify MCP server and Apify AI share the same Actor search and execution backend, but they serve different audiences:

- MCP server - a programmatic interface for external AI agents, IDEs, and CLIs. Use it when you build or operate your own agent.
- Apify AI - the conversational interface inside Apify Console for users who interact with Apify through a chat UI rather than their own agent.

Actor ranking on both surfaces uses parameters similar to those evaluated by the Actor quality score, so Actors with higher quality scores tend to rank higher.

## Excluded Actors

Due to security reasons, the MCP server intentionally excludes full-permission Actors from search and execution. Running a full-permission Actor is a decision you approve personally, so an LLM can't make it on your behalf.

## Prerequisites

Before connecting your AI to Apify, you need:

- An Apify account - You need one unless your agent uses only the tools that work without an account or pays through agentic payments. Sign up for an Apify account, if you don't have one.
- MCP client - An AI agent or client that supports Model Context Protocol (MCP). This could be claude.ai, Claude Desktop, VS Code with MCP support, or any application that implements the MCP specification. The official MCP documentation maintains a list of compatible clients.
- Apify API token (optional) - Only needed for the local stdio server or the Bearer token option. The recommended remote connection signs you in with OAuth instead. Create an API token in Apify Console.

## Connect and authorize

To discover Actors and search the documentation, you can connect without an account. To run Actors, connect in one of two ways: use the hosted Apify service with Streamable HTTP with OAuth, or run the server locally for development and testing with local stdio.

Structured output schemas

The hosted Apify MCP server at `https://mcp.apify.com` supports output schema inference for structured Actor results. Actor tools automatically include inferred output schemas with field-level type information. This helps AI agents understand the expected result structure before calling an Actor. The local stdio server does not support this feature.

### Use without an account

The Apify MCP server accepts requests without an API token when the `tools` query parameter (see Tool selection) contains only tools enabled for unauthenticated use. These tools cover Actor discovery, documentation lookup, and the Apify API reference:

- `search-actors`
- `fetch-actor-details`
- `search-apify-docs`
- `fetch-apify-docs`
- `apify-api-search`
- `apify-api-details`

For example, the following URL connects without authentication:

`https://mcp.apify.com?tools=search-actors,fetch-actor-details,search-apify-docs,fetch-apify-docs`

If the `tools` parameter includes any other tool, or you connect to the default endpoint, the server requires an API token. Running Actors and accessing storage or run data always requires authentication, so use one of the methods below when you're ready to run Actors.

### Streamable HTTP with OAuth (recommended)

Add `https://mcp.apify.com` to your MCP client. On first connection, your browser opens so you can sign in to Apify and approve access. To authorize without signing in, use your Apify API token instead.

OAuth

This flow authorizes the server without putting your API token in the client configuration.

```json
{

  "mcpServers": {

    "apify": {

      "url": "https://mcp.apify.com"

    }

  }

}

```

Bearer token

You can also use your Apify token directly, instead of OAuth, by setting the `Authorization: Bearer ` header in the MCP server configuration.

```json
{

  "mcpServers": {

    "apify": {

      "url": "https://mcp.apify.com",

      "headers": {

        "Authorization": "Bearer <APIFY_TOKEN>"

      }

    }

  }

}

```

Replace `` with your Apify API token.

For a client-specific configuration, use the MCP configurator: pick the Actors and tools you need, then copy the generated configuration into your client. If you use the Apify CLI, `apify mcp install ` writes the configuration for you, for example `apify mcp install cursor`.

### Local stdio

If your client doesn't support remote MCP servers using the `https://mcp.apify.com` URL, you can run the server locally instead. This method uses the stdio transport to connect directly through your local environment.

Add this to your configuration file:

```json
{

  "mcpServers": {

    "actors-mcp-server": {

      "command": "npx",

      "args": ["-y", "@apify/actors-mcp-server"],

      "env": {

        "APIFY_TOKEN": "YOUR_APIFY_TOKEN"

      }

    }

  }

}

```

The server will download automatically on first use and connect using your API token.

## Tool selection

By default, the MCP server loads the `actors` and `docs` tool categories, the `apify/web-search` and `apify/web-fetch` Actors, and `report-problem`. To choose different tools, set the `tools` parameter in the server URL. The parameter replaces the default selection instead of adding to it, so list everything you want to load:

`https://mcp.apify.com?tools=actors,docs,apify/web-search,apify/web-fetch`

For instance, `https://mcp.apify.com?tools=storage` loads only the storage tools, without `search-actors` or `call-actor`. The default Actors don't belong to any category, so `?tools=actors,docs` also drops them.

For minimal setups where you only need specific Actors:

`https://mcp.apify.com?tools=apify/instagram-scraper,apify/google-search-scraper`

Each Actor you select with the `tools` parameter becomes a tool of its own, named `{username}--{actor-name}`. For example, the server exposes `apify/web-search` as `apify--web-search`. The server replaces dots in the username with `-dot-` and shortens names longer than 64 characters by adding a hash suffix to keep them unique.

This configuration approach works for both hosted and local setups. For the CLI version:

`npx @apify/actors-mcp-server --tools actors,docs,apify/web-scraper`

To select your tools visually, use the MCP configurator, then copy the generated configuration to your client.

### Available tools

| Tool name | Category | Enabled by default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `search-actors` | `actors` | ✅ | Search for Actors in Apify Store |
| `fetch-actor-details` | `actors` | ✅ | Retrieve detailed information about a specific Actor, including its input and output schema, README (summary when available, full otherwise), and pricing |
| `call-actor` | `actors` | ✅ | Run an Actor and wait up to `waitSecs` (0-45, default 30) for it to finish. Pass run limits (`memory`, `timeout`, `maxItems`, `maxTotalChargeUsd`) in `callOptions`, not in the Actor input. Returns the run status and storage IDs, not the results themselves |
| `fetch-actor-mcp-tool-list` | `actors` | ✅ | List the tools of an Actor that runs an MCP server, with their schemas, annotations, and metadata |
| `call-actor-mcp-tool` | `actors` | ✅ | Call one tool on an Actor's MCP server and return its result |
| `send-server-actor-request` | `actors` | ✅ | Send one HTTP request to a Server Actor's API, as documented by its API schema, and return the response |
| apify/web-search | Actor | ✅ | Search the web and return the results in the response, without starting an Actor run |
| apify/web-fetch | Actor | ✅ | Fetch one http(s) URL and return its full content, rendering JavaScript and bypassing anti-bot protection |
| apify/rag-web-browser | Actor |  | Search the web and return the content of the top results |
| `search-apify-docs` | `docs` | ✅ | Search the Apify documentation for relevant pages |
| `fetch-apify-docs` | `docs` | ✅ | Fetch the full content of an Apify documentation page by its URL |

...

Your AI can search Apify Store for relevant Actors using the `search-actors` tool, inspect Actor details to understand required inputs, and call any Actor by name using `call-actor` - without needing to pre-configure it. This means your AI can adapt to new tasks without manual configuration.

...

The MCP server collects telemetry data about tool calls and MCP clients to help Apify understand usage patterns and improve the service. Participation in this program is optional and you may opt out if you prefer not to share any information.

### Data collection

All telemetry data is collected and stored securely. We do not collect any sensitive information such as conversations, arguments passed to tools, API tokens, or personal data.

The server collects anonymous information about tool usage, including:

- Basic information about used tools (calls, success/failure, duration)
- MCP client attributes (client name, version, capabilities)

By default, telemetry is enabled for all tool calls.

highlights:
# Apify MCP server

Connect your agent to the largest marketplace of tools for AI.

**The official Apify Model Context Protocol (MCP) server gives AI agents web scraping, data extraction, and browser automation through thousands of ready-made Actors from Apify Store, at `https://mcp.apify.com`.**

Apify is the marketplace of ready-to-run tools for AI agents. One connection to the Apify MCP server gives your agent thousands of tools to choose from, for jobs like web fetch, SERP monitoring, lead generation and enrichment, and pulling data from e-commerce sites and social media. The server loads only what each task needs.

Your agent searches Apify Store, checks an Actor's input and pricing, runs it, and reads the structured results, so you don't install a separate MCP server for every site. Connect to the hosted server with OAuth, or run it locally over stdio with the `@apify/actors-mcp-server` npm package.

...

## 🚀 Quickstart

1. Open the MCP configurator, pick your client, and choose the tools you want.
2. Copy the generated configuration, deeplink, or command into your client.
3. Sign in to Apify in the browser window that opens. If you don't have an account, you can create a free one there.

The hosted endpoint is `https://mcp.apify.com`. If your client can't use OAuth, send your Apify API token in an `Authorization: Bearer <APIFY_TOKEN>` header instead. Treat the token like a password and keep it out of repositories. Create a token in Apify Console and copy it right after creating it. It is shown only once.

Using a coding agent such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or GitHub Copilot? An official Apify plugin installs this MCP server together with Apify agent skills in one step.

...

## Remote (hosted) or local MCP server

The hosted remote MCP server with OAuth is the recommended option. Use the local server when you want to run the MCP process on your own machine; Actors still run and store their results on the Apify platform in both modes. If your client supports only stdio, you can also bridge it to the hosted server with `mcp-remote`: `npx mcp-remote https://mcp.apify.com`.

| | Hosted (`https://mcp.apify.com`) | Local (`npx @apify/actors-mcp-server`) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Transport | Streamable HTTP | stdio |
| Authentication | OAuth or Bearer token | `APIFY_TOKEN` environment variable or Apify CLI login |
| Output schemas inferred for Actor results | Yes | No |
| Tool selection | `tools` URL parameter | `--tools` flag or `TOOLS` environment variable |
| Updates | Always the latest server | The npm version you install |

## How an agent uses Apify Actors

Actors are serverless programs on the Apify platform. Each one does a specific job, like scraping Google Maps, crawling a website for RAG, or collecting social media posts. The MCP server turns Actors into tools an agent can find and call without you configuring each one in advance.

A typical task follows four steps:

1. `search-actors` finds candidate Actors in Apify Store for the task.
2. `fetch-actor-details` returns the Actor's input schema, README, and pricing, plus its output schema on request.
3. `call-actor` starts the run and waits for it to finish, 30 seconds by default and up to 45. It returns the **run status and storage IDs**; the scraped items stay in the run's dataset.
4. `get-dataset-items` reads the results from the run's dataset, with `limit` and `offset` for pagination.

The server adds `get-dataset-items`, `get-key-value-store-record`, `get-actor-run`, and `abort-actor-run` whenever `call-actor` or an Actor tool is loaded, so the agent can always read results and check on long runs that outlast the wait.

You can also expose a specific Actor as its own tool, for example `apify/instagram-scraper`. The server builds the tool's parameters from the Actor's input schema, so the agent knows exactly what to pass. A Server Actor with an API schema, such as `apify/web-fetch`, `apify/web-search`, or `apify/rag-web-browser`, gets a tool that sends one HTTP request to its API instead.

**Actors that run their own MCP server.** Some Actors are MCP servers themselves. `fetch-actor-mcp-tool-list` lists their tools, and `call-actor-mcp-tool` calls one. When such an Actor is loaded as a tool source and has no API schema, its tools are exposed under names in the form `username--actor-name--tool-name`; an Actor with an API schema, such as `apify/web-search`, gets its server tool instead, and `call-actor-mcp-tool` reaches its MCP tools. Apify Store also lists MCP-related Actors from independent creators; those are separate products with their own READMEs and pricing.

...

By default, the server loads the `actors` and `docs` categories, two Actor tools (Web Search and Web Fetch), and `report-problem`. Everything else is opt-in by category or by tool name.

...

| Tool name | Category | Description | Enabled by default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :---: |
| `search-actors` | actors | Search for Actors in Apify Store. | ✅ |
| `fetch-actor-details` | actors | Get an Actor's input schema, README (summary when available, full otherwise), pricing, and a Server Actor's HTTP operations. The output schema is opt-in. | ✅ |
| `call-actor` | actors | Run an Actor and return its run status and storage IDs. Use `fetch-actor-details` first to get the input schema. | ✅ |
| `fetch-actor-mcp-tool-list` | actors | List the tools of an Actor that runs an MCP server, with their schemas,

...

| `call-actor-mcp-tool` | actors | Call one tool on an Actor's MCP server and return its result. | ✅ |

...

An MCP server exposes tools and data to AI agents through the Model Context Protocol, an open standard supported by clients such as Claude, ChatGPT, and Cursor.
